entities.name: PMID:25448630
observations: Xinjiang case-control comparison included 800 ethnic Kazakhs and 800 Han Chinese adults with essential hypertension or healthy controls.

CMV serology and gB genotyping were assessed; CMV seropositivity was independently associated with hypertension in Kazakh males, while CMV antibody titers were associated with hypertension and blood pressure in Han participants.
The gB2+gB3 genotype mixture was independently associated with hypertension in Kazakh females; exact adjusted effect estimates were unavailable in the retrieved abstract.

entities.name: PMID:29752343
observations: Xinjiang case-control analysis included 720 ethnic Kazakhs, 360 with essential hypertension and 360 controls.

Hypertension cases had higher HCMV seropositivity than controls (P=0.04); HCMV IgG titers correlated with blood pressure and inflammatory, oxidative-stress, endothelial, renin, and methylation markers.
The study supports an HCMV–essential hypertension association in ethnic Kazakhs, but exact adjusted effect estimates were unavailable in the retrieved record.

entities.name: PMID:28837559
observations: Xinjiang study included 563 Han Chinese participants: 372 hypertensive patients and 191 healthy controls.
CMV IgG was higher in essential hypertension, increased with hypertension grade and target-organ damage, and positively correlated with arterial blood pressure.
CMV IgG thresholds above 4.25 U and 4.85 U were reported as independent predictors of hypertension progression and target-organ damage, respectively.

entities.name: Essential hypertension
observations: In the directly relevant Xinjiang ethnic-Kazakh and Han Chinese studies, HCMV infection markers or antibody burden were consistently associated with essential hypertension.
The evidence is observational and supports association rather than proving that HCMV causes essential hypertension.

entities.name: Human cytomegalovirus
observations: HCMV seropositivity, IgG antibody titers, and selected gB genotypes were associated with essential hypertension in ethnic Kazakh and Han Chinese Xinjiang study populations.
No distinct Kazakhstan-resident national cohort was identified; the Kazakh evidence concerns ethnic Kazakhs living in Xinjiang, China.
